questions.prompt: What is the idiomatic way to type a component's props in <script setup>?
questions.explanation: defineProps<{ ... }>() declares typed props at compile time; withDefaults adds defaults (object/array defaults require a factory function).

questions.prompt: Why can't plain tsc type-check your Vue components?

options.text: tsc doesn't understand the .vue single-file component format; you need vue-tsc
You must compile to JavaScript first by hand

questions.explanation: .vue SFCs need a Vue-aware checker. vue-tsc (and Volar in the editor) understand SFCs; plain tsc skips them.

questions.prompt: How do you type a template ref to a child component instance?
questions.explanation: InstanceType<typeof Comp> is the component instance type; the ref is null until mount, so include | null. You can only access members the child exposed via defineExpose.

questions.prompt: The Vue-aware tool that type-checks .vue files (used in this project's build) is vue-______. (complete the word)
questions.explanation: vue-tsc type-checks single-file components; this project runs vue-tsc -b before vite build.

questions.prompt: How do you make a component generic so its props relate by type?

options.text: Add the generic attribute: <script setup lang="ts" generic="T">

questions.explanation: Since Vue 3.3, the generic attribute on <script setup> lets you use a type parameter T across defineProps and defineEmits so related props share a type.

questions.prompt: What's a correct way to give a type-based array prop a default value?
questions.explanation: Object and array prop defaults must be returned from a factory function to avoid sharing one instance across components: { tags: () => [] }.
